sections.heading: Flat Roof FAQs for Montclair Homeowners

faqs.q: How long does a flat roof last in Montclair, NJ?

runs.v: EPDM rubber lasts 15 to 25 years, TPO 7 to 20 years, modified bitumen 20 years, and built-up roofing 30 years, per the InterNACHI life-expectancy chart, if ponding drains off in under two days.

faqs.q: Why does water pond on my Montclair flat roof, and is it a problem?

runs.v: Water ponds when the slope drops below ¼ inch per foot, and ponding that stays more than 48 hours is a defect that breaks down seams, per the NRCA and ARMA; tapered insulation and clear drains fix it.

faqs.q: Which flat-roof membrane should I choose for my Montclair building?

runs.v: It depends on use, exposure, and drainage: white TPO cuts cooling load on a sunny deck, EPDM offers single-ply durability, and modified bitumen suits storefront decks that see foot traffic.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit for a flat roof in Montclair?

runs.v: Not for the covering on a detached one- or two-family home, which is ordinary maintenance under N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7. New Jersey's construction code has specific requirements for roofing installations, and major roof installations or replacements on commercial, multi-family, or attached buildings need a building permit once work exceeds 25% of the roof area in 12 months. That is the 25% rule for roofing in NJ code, and roofers also treat about 25% damage as the point where replacement beats repair; confirm with the Montclair construction office.

faqs.q: What's the best way to fix a flat roof?

runs.v: Find the real failure first, usually a seam, flashing, or ponding, then repair it with the same membrane and correct the drainage; a patch over wet insulation fails again.
